b1-review-2.R2.1 Thanksgiving at the hostel:
Mrs. Lima: Danny, the table looks wonderful! Who taught you to cook a turkey?
Danny: Nobody! I'd never cooked one before. My mom explained everything on the phone. She said, don't take it out of the oven until it's golden.
Ana: Well, it's perfect. Could you tell me what's in the stuffing? It's delicious.
Danny: Bread, onions, celery and herbs. And no nuts, of course!
Bruno: Hey, look out the window. Someone in the building across the street is waving at us.
Ana: It must be your neighbor. She's always at that window.
Mrs. Lima: It can't be her. She's visiting her daughter this week. It might be one of my old guests.
Danny: Whoever it is, happy Thanksgiving! In the US, it's on the fourth Thursday of November. Families get together, eat too much and say what they're thankful for.
Bruno: OK, but you'd better sit down first. You've been cooking all day.
Ana: And how's your ankle, Bruno?
Bruno: Much better, thanks. The doctor said I should rest for two weeks, but I'd rather run than sit at home. I've been running again since Monday.
Ana: So now most of the people at this table are runners!
Mrs. Lima: Not me. I prefer cooking to running. Danny, is that sweater new?
Danny: No, it was bought second-hand. It was made in the nineteen nineties! And the coat on my chair was sent by Paulo. It's a bit too big for me, but it's warm enough for my trip south.
Ana: My brother never wears anything twice. He always buys a new one!
Bruno: Mrs. Lima, tell Ana how you met your husband.
Mrs. Lima: Oh, again? He had just arrived from Recife, and he came to my father's bakery every morning for one bread roll. I had never seen such a shy man!
Danny: OK, everyone. As soon as you finish the turkey, there's pumpkin pie. It's my comfort food. It reminds me of home.
Ana: Danny, I'm thankful you're here. Even when you get the flu!
